recipes.title: Paint the whole page
recipes.summary: FujiProvider paints only its own wrapper, so a short page or the area past it stays the browser's white in dark mode.
steps: Give the root provider a full-height class, so its themed background fills the viewport.

Add `persist` to the root provider (and the bootstrap script for SSR - see the `persist` recipe): it mirrors the appearance onto <html>, which then takes the theme background and color-scheme, so overscroll and scrollbars match too.
Never add a second full-page background of your own; `--fuji-background` already switches with the theme.
gotchas: Nested providers are isolated preview scopes: they never touch <html>, and only the root provider should set `persist`.

recipes.title: A light/dark toggle
recipes.summary: Read and change the theme with useFujiConfig() from any component inside the provider.
steps: Render the toggle inside FujiProvider - outside it, useFujiConfig() returns fixed defaults and a no-op setter.
Uncontrolled provider (`defaultTheme`) plus `setTheme` is the simplest form; the provider owns the state.
To own the state yourself, pass `theme` with `onThemeChange` instead - never both `theme` and `defaultTheme`.
gotchas: Do not toggle a `.dark` class or write `data-fuji-theme` on <html> yourself: the provider owns those attributes and overwrites them on its next render.

recipes.title: Follow the operating system
recipes.summary: There is no theme="system" value. Read prefers-color-scheme and pass the result as a controlled theme.
steps: Subscribe to the media query with useSyncExternalStore, so the theme updates live when the OS switches.
Pass it as the controlled `theme`; the server snapshot must be a fixed value so hydration matches.
gotchas: With server rendering a dark-OS visitor sees one light frame before hydration. To avoid it, offer an explicit choice instead and use the `persist` recipe.

recipes.title: Remember the choice without a flash
recipes.summary: `persist` saves theme, material, radius and elevation to localStorage; with SSR a pre-paint script applies them before hydration.
steps: Set `persist` on the root provider only.
Client-only apps (Vite, CRA): nothing else - the provider applies the saved value before the first paint.
Server-rendered apps (Next.js): add the script from buildAppearanceBootstrapScript() to <head>, with the same defaults as the provider, and mark <html> suppressHydrationWarning and data-fuji-boot.
gotchas: The script's defaults and the provider's default* props must match, or a first-time visitor flips between them.
Never hand-copy the script or its storage key (`fuji-appearance`): the export is kept in step with what `persist` writes.

recipes.title: Glass
recipes.summary: material="glass" layers translucency and blur over the active theme; the theme is the glass tint. It needs something behind it to show.
steps: Turn it on at the provider: material="glass" (or defaultMaterial / setMaterial). Keep theme as is - dark + glass and light + glass are both valid.
Put a backdrop behind it. Over the theme's flat background glass is correct but subtle; add the shipped `fuji-glass-atmosphere` class to a full-height wrapper, or your own photo or gradient.
Panels, sidebars, overlays and cards take the material; buttons, fields and other controls stay solid on purpose.
For one region in a different tint (a bright photo under a dark app), nest a provider with its own theme AND material - nested providers inherit no axes.
gotchas: There is no glassTint prop and no theme="glass" value; both were removed.
Under prefers-reduced-transparency, or where backdrop-filter is unsupported, glass falls back to opaque surfaces automatically.
Text over your own busy photo needs the stronger surfaces: prefer --fuji-surface or --fuji-surface-raised over --fuji-surface-subtle.

recipes.title: Make your own markup follow the theme
recipes.summary: Hard-coded colours (bg-white, text-gray-900) and Tailwind's dark: variant do not follow FujiProvider. Use the --fuji-* tokens.
steps: Style app-owned elements with the tokens, which switch with theme and material: var(--fuji-background), var(--fuji-surface), var(--fuji-foreground), var(--fuji-foreground-muted), var(--fuji-border).
With Tailwind v4, map the tokens once so utilities like bg-fuji-surface exist in your own build (the package's compiled classes are prefixed and not meant for your markup).
If you use Tailwind's dark: variant, point it at Fuji's theme attribute so it follows the provider instead of the OS.
gotchas: Without Tailwind, use the variables directly: `.panel { background: var(--fuji-surface); color: var(--fuji-foreground); }`.
Tailwind v3: darkMode: ["selector", '[data-fuji-theme="dark"]'] in tailwind.config does the same as the @custom-variant line.
Call get_appearance with topic "tokens" for the full token list and each theme's values.

recipes.title: Design tokens
recipes.summary: Every --fuji-* custom property, grouped. Values switch per theme and material; pass `group` to list one group with its values.
steps: Colour: --fuji-background, --fuji-surface(-subtle|-strong|-raised|-overlay), --fuji-foreground(-muted|-subtle), --fuji-border(-strong), and the tones --fuji-default|forest|sun|fire|water with -foreground, -soft and -border.
Reach for -raised when a fill carries text or an icon, -strong only for a bare fill (a track, a divider).
Override a token by redeclaring it on .fuji-theme-scope (or a narrower element); check contrast in both themes and both materials.
